Research

Research

PRADA-X Lab

Medical Imaging Classification
  • Adapted and implemented a CNN-based binary image classification pipeline in PyTorch, evaluating how colormap selection affects diagnostic model performance across 3 architectures (InceptionNetV3, MobileNetV2, ResNet50) on two medical imaging datasets
  • Iteratively refined training configurations through systematic hyperparameter tuning using stratified 5-fold cross-validation, improving AUPROC from baseline to 0.852 and AUROC to 0.821 on erythema detection
  • Designed data cleansing and visualization pipeline using Grad-CAM heatmaps and binary segmentation masks for model interpretability
  • Applied data augmentation techniques including rotation, flipping, color jitter, and gaussian blur to address class imbalance and improve model generalization across limited medical imaging datasets
  • Computed Intersection over Union (IoU) between Grad-CAM regions and ground truth masks to quantitatively assess model interpretability
  • Automated colormap preprocessing and model evaluation workflows to enable systematic benchmarking across multiple datasets
  • Conducted ablation study across colormap configurations, evaluating model performance using AUPROC, AUROC, F1, sensitivity, and specificity metrics to identify optimal input representations for erythema and breast cancer detection
PyTorch CNNs Scikit-learn Model Evaluation Feature Engineering Hyperparameter Tuning Data Augmentation Deep Learning Grad-CAM IoU
